newsitem.title: USA: Former AT&T exec settles insider trading suit.
newsitem.headline: Former AT&T exec settles insider trading suit.

text.p: A former executive of AT&T Corp has agreed to pay $813,600 in penalties to settle charges that he and a friend orchestrated an insider trading scheme on stocks of AT&T takeover targets, regulators said.

Charles Brumfield, a former AT&T labour relations vice-president in Morristown, New Jersey, agreed to the settlement without admitting or denying allegations, the Securities and Exchange Commission said on Monday.

The SEC charged Brumfield and his friend, Thomas Alger, in February 1995 for allegedly orchestrating trading of stocks of four AT&T targets: NCR Corp, Digital Microwave Corp, Paradyne Corp and Teradata Corp.
The scheme which extended from December 1988 to about 1993, is believed to have netted their participants about $2.6 million in illegal profits.
Brumfield and Alger allegedly gave "tips" to the other accused, who traded on the information. Later, the two received kickbacks of about $300,000 from the "tippees," the SEC said.
